prep_aptitude_questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 12 days and B can do it in 18 days. If they work together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: A’s 1-day work = 1/12. B’s 1-day work = 1/18. Combined 1-day work = 1/12 + 1/18 = (3+2)/36 = 5/36. Total days = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

prep_aptitude_questions.question: A train running at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a 200m long platform in 22 seconds. What is the length of the train?
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: Speed = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Total distance in 22s = 20 * 22 = 440m. Length of train = 440 - 200 = 240 meters.

prep_aptitude_questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an item 25% above cost price and allows a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage?
In how many different ways can the letters of the word "ENGINE" be arranged?
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: ENGINE has 6 letters: E appears 2 times, N appears 2 times, G appears 1 time, I appears 1 time. Total arrangements = 6! / (2! * 2!) = 720 / 4 = 180.

prep_aptitude_questions.question: Look at this series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ... What number comes next?
Statements: All computers are machines. Some machines are smart. Conclusions: I. Some computers are smart. II. Some machines are computers.
prep_aptitude_questions.options: ["Only conclusion I follows","Only conclusion II follows","Both I and II follow","Neither I nor II follows"]
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: Since all computers are machines, some machines are definitely computers (Conclusion II). There is no guaranteed overlap between computers and smart machines.

prep_aptitude_questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Rohit said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the girl related to Rohit?
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: Rohit’s grandfather’s only son is Rohit’s father. The daughter of Rohit’s father is Rohit’s sister.

prep_aptitude_questions.question: If "CLOUD" is coded as "ENQWF", what will "RAIN" be coded as in the same code?
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted by +2: R(+2)->T, A(+2)->C, I(+2)->K, N(+2)->P => TCKP.

prep_aptitude_questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to "CANDID":
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward. Deceitful is the direct antonym.

prep_aptitude_questions.question: Identify the error: "Neither of the two candidates (A) / were selected (B) / for the executive role (C) / No error (D)"
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: "Neither" takes a singular verb. The correct phrasing is "was selected" instead of "were selected".

prep_aptitude_questions.question: Select the synonym for "METICULOUS":
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise (Diligent).

prep_aptitude_questions.question: Fill in the blank: "The committee has submitted its report _____ the board for review."
prep_aptitude_questions.explanation: "Submit to" is the standard prepositional phrase used when submitting documentation to an authority.
